title: Oil Holds Gain as Traders Weigh Signals of Near-Term Tightness
content: Oil held a gain after US data showed the world’s largest economy holding up despite the fallout from the Washington-led trade war, while crude market metrics pointed to near-term tightness.

title: China Injects Most Short-Term Cash This Week Since January
content: China ramped up its short-term cash injection into the banking system to the highest since January this week as it sought to replenish funds drained by tax payments and heavy government debt issuance.

content: A once-popular trade that drew foreign funds into Chinese onshore bonds is losing its appeal, threatening to trigger an extended bout of outflows.

content: Malaysia appointed Court of Appeal judge Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh as the new chief justice of the Federal Court, ending a two-week vacancy that had sparked concerns over the independence of the judiciary.

content: India’s top private-sector banks HDFC Bank Ltd. and ICICI Bank Ltd. could see profits come under pressure from loan growth at a three-year low and thinning margins driven by central bank rate cuts, as they report earnings this weekend.

title: US Set to Impose 93.5% Duty on China Battery Material

content: Fukoku Life Insurance may increase its purchases of Japanese super-long bonds just as the nation’s debt market trembled this week ahead of upper house elections.

title: Waller Explains Why the Fed Should Cut Rates Now

Speaking during an event hosted by the Money Marketeers in New York, Waller also says the Trump administration has not talked to him about replacing Fed Chair Jerome Powell.

title: Netflix Tops Wall Street’s Lofty Estimates
content:
While rival media companies are unloading assets and cutting costs, Netflix Inc. continues to thrive.
The owner of the world’s most popular paid streaming service on Thursday reported second-quarter results that exceeded investor expectations in every major metric, saying revenue grew to $11.1 billion and earnings jumped to $7.19 a share. The company also raised its forecast for full-year sales and profit margins. The second quarter is historically slow for Netflix, which typically adds more customers at the beginning and end of the year.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Invesco Aims to Unlock Hundreds of Millions in Profit From QQQ
content: It’s a quirk in the booming world of passive investing: Famed tech fund QQQ is the most profitable offering in the $11.7 trillion ETF industry, but Invesco Ltd. earns virtually nothing from running it. Now the asset manager is asking shareholders to change that.

title: Netflix Thrives as Estimates Topped, Forecast Raised
content: Netflix reported second-quarter results that exceeded investor expectations in every major metric. The company raised its forecast for full-year sales and profit margins, expecting to generate up to $45.2 billion in sales and an operating margin of 29.5%. Bloomberg Intelligence’s Geetha Ranganathan has more on “Bloomberg The Close.”

title: Netflix Theme Parks to Open Later This Year
content: Later this year Netflix is expected to open two theme parks called Netflix House, one in Philadelphia and one in Dallas.  Len Testa, President of Touring Plans, which helps customers plan park and cruise trips, joins “The Close” to discuss what he expects from this new direction for Netflix. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Couche-Tard’s Failed Bid for Seven & i Sparks Debate Over Japan
content: Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.’s decision to walk away in frustration from an attempted acquisition of Seven & i Holdings Co. set off a debate in Tokyo as to what lessons foreign companies with ambitions for M&A should draw.

title: Disneyland Opens | On This Day
content: 70 years ago on July 17, 1955 Disneyland in Anaheim California opened it’s doors. Many theme parks followed like Universal Studios, Legoland, and now Netflix House. Romaine Bostick has more on the future of them parks. (Source: Bloomberg)
